Projects, demos, and tools built with Jev.

Jev answers questions about data: pick an option, return a yes/no probability, or score something on a scale. It does not write text. The examples here show what people are using it for, with links to the code where available.

45 reviewed picks. Source notes and licenses. The larger discovery catalog is separate.

Quick start · Projects · Demos from X · CUA & drivers · OpenRouter winners · Contributing

Check permissions and data handling before running a project. A listing here is not a security audit.

20-second quick-start

Install typesafe-sdk and set TYPESAFE_API_KEY in your environment. This example makes one paid request:

from typesafe_sdk import Choice, TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    result = client.system_one(
        state={"document": "I was charged twice."},
        questions={"team": Choice(
            instructions="Which team should handle this ticket?",
            criteria={"billing": None, "technical": None, "other": None},
        )},
    )
print(result.choices["team"].choice)  # e.g. billing; actual output can differ

No key yet? python3 examples/route_ticket.py prints the request without calling the API. SDK setup.

Start with a classifier, an agent, or a local alternative.

For simple rules, parsing, or arithmetic, use code. A dedicated classifier may be a better fit for a fixed task. Jev is worth trying when the choices change or the input is messy; test it on your own examples rather than relying on a demo's timing.

Reviewed picks

SDKs and skills

  • TypeSafe JavaScript SDK - Official JavaScript and TypeScript client.
  • TypeSafe Python SDK - Official Python client, with a support-ticket routing example.
  • Jev Logs - Scores log entries with Jev to decide which need a closer look.
  • Jevify - Agent skill for finding places to use Jev and planning comparisons with existing code.
  • Official TypeSafe skill - Official skill for writing Jev requests and choosing between Noul, Choice, and Score.
  • Skillbox - Self-hosted skill library with optional Jev-based recommendations.
  • Tenbin - MCP server and skill for linting Jev questions, evaluating labeled examples, and choosing decision thresholds.
  • wellposed - Offline linter and agent skill for Jev requests: checks missing options, broken state references, and question types.
  • jevrs - Async Rust client with typed answers, derive macros, and native or WASI transports.

Browser and desktop tools

  • Cua Driver + jev-use - Cua Driver example in Python and TypeScript: Jev chooses an action, the driver runs it, and code checks the result.
  • Jev Browser (MCP, CLI, library) - Playwright browser controlled by Jev, available as an MCP server, CLI, or library.
  • Jev Browser Skill - Small browser-control reference showing how to build and execute Jev action choices.
  • Jev Browser Use (existing Codex connection) - Skill that uses an existing Codex browser connection. Jev clicks and scrolls; Codex types and checks the result.
  • Jev Cua (Codex/Waku) - Mac automation using Cua Driver, with optional Jev recommendations for saved workflows.
  • Jev Social - Read-only Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn research loop: Jev Choice questions pick the platform and each bounded search, read, inspect, or finish operation; SocAI executes in the user's Chrome and the app retains source-linked evidence.
  • Jev Ultrafast - Jev picks browser actions and page elements; a separate model writes text.
  • Jev voice browser - Voice-controlled Playwright browser. Jev chooses actions from partial speech and page controls.
  • jev-bot (@compootor) - Native Mac controls through a JavaScript MCP session, with optional Jev element selection.
  • TypeSafe computer use (macOS) - Mac automation using local OCR and accessibility data, with Jev choosing the next action.

Agent tools

  • Foreman - Uses Jev to check a coding agent's progress and decide when it needs intervention.
  • Jev MCP - MCP tools for checking claims against evidence, screening content, and ranking candidates.
  • jev-belay - Claude Code Stop hook that checks local run evidence before Jev judges an unverified completion claim.
  • jev-claude-statusline - Claude Code hooks send task text, recent tool summaries, latest assistant message, and turn status to Jev (Score phase plus Noul done/waiting_on_user); answers are cached and shown as a progress segment on the Claude Code status line.
  • jev_search - Ranks files by keyword, then checks their passages with Jev in two passes. Author marks it experimental.
  • jgrep (npm: jevgrep) - Jev answers one Noul per code chunk, diff hunk, or CSV row (does this match the description?); code prints the probabilities as file:line hits, gates CI on an English rule with --diff, and lists the test files a diff can affect with --tests.
  • Oko - Code-search CLI and MCP server that finds candidates locally and uses Jev to rank the source snippets.
  • TypeSafe MCP - Go MCP server for making Jev requests from coding agents.

Apps and integrations

  • nospace - Adds spaces while you type. Jev chooses between possible word splits; a separate model handles spelling corrections.
  • tisco - Searches video transcripts with Jev, then previews clip moves and renames for approval.
  • Vibe Domain - Ranks domain names by the requested style. Has a no-key heuristic mode and a hosted Jev option.
  • Home Assistant Jev - Adds Jev decisions to Home Assistant entities and automations.
  • llm-typesafe - Use Jev from the LLM command line or Python, with stdin, templates, and sync/async calls.
  • MinusPodJev - Podcast ad-detection adapter for MinusPod: Jev scores transcript segments and code assembles the ad spans.

Games and creative projects

  • Jev Chess - A shared chess game against Jev with move probabilities. Hosted demo; source code not verified.
  • Jev Plays Snake - Snake where code finds legal moves and Jev picks a direction.
  • jev-plays-pokemon-red - Pokemon Red agent where code builds legal actions and route state; Jev chooses only at branch points.
  • JevAI for XMage - Magic: The Gathering bots that use Jev alone or alongside XMage search.
  • JevPilot - Driving simulation where Jev chooses steering and speed. Not a real-world driving system.
  • PROMPT FPS / Jev Doom - Jev chooses actions in a browser-based Doom engine. Uses Freedoom assets.
  • TypeSafe Mario - Jev picks controller inputs from emulator state. Requires a lawful local game setup.
  • Jev Music Playground - Jev picks musical parameters; code turns them into notes and MIDI. Includes an offline mode.

Independent models

  • CUA-S1-FORMS (independent specialist) - Cua's independent form-filling model and dataset. Not a general desktop agent or official Jev weights.
  • Jevlike (independent option scorer) - Independent one-pass option scorer with training code and game examples. Not TypeSafe Jev.
  • OpenJev SGLang - Independent typed-decision server using open models and SGLang. Not official Jev weights.

Supporting drivers

  • Browser Harness (supporting driver) - The CDP browser connection used by Jev Ultrafast. Model-neutral, not a Jev model.

Projects, demos, and tools built with Jev.

Jev answers questions about data: pick an option, return a yes/no probability, or score something on a scale. It does not write text. The examples here show what people are using it for, with links to the code where available.

45 reviewed picks. Source notes and licenses. The larger discovery catalog is separate.

Quick start · Projects · Demos from X · CUA & drivers · OpenRouter winners · Contributing

Check permissions and data handling before running a project. A listing here is not a security audit.

20-second quick-start

Install typesafe-sdk and set TYPESAFE_API_KEY in your environment. This example makes one paid request:

from typesafe_sdk import Choice, TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    result = client.system_one(
        state={"document": "I was charged twice."},
        questions={"team": Choice(
            instructions="Which team should handle this ticket?",
            criteria={"billing": None, "technical": None, "other": None},
        )},
    )
print(result.choices["team"].choice)  # e.g. billing; actual output can differ

No key yet? python3 examples/route_ticket.py prints the request without calling the API. SDK setup.

Start with a classifier, an agent, or a local alternative.

For simple rules, parsing, or arithmetic, use code. A dedicated classifier may be a better fit for a fixed task. Jev is worth trying when the choices change or the input is messy; test it on your own examples rather than relying on a demo's timing.

Browser Use / @gregpr07. Author recording, not our benchmark. Implementation · More demos and videos.

Reviewed picks

SDKs and skills

  • TypeSafe JavaScript SDK - Official JavaScript and TypeScript client.
  • TypeSafe Python SDK - Official Python client, with a support-ticket routing example.
  • Jev Logs - Scores log entries with Jev to decide which need a closer look.
  • Jevify - Agent skill for finding places to use Jev and planning comparisons with existing code.
  • Official TypeSafe skill - Official skill for writing Jev requests and choosing between Noul, Choice, and Score.
  • Skillbox - Self-hosted skill library with optional Jev-based recommendations.
  • Tenbin - MCP server and skill for linting Jev questions, evaluating labeled examples, and choosing decision thresholds.
  • wellposed - Offline linter and agent skill for Jev requests: checks missing options, broken state references, and question types.
  • jevrs - Async Rust client with typed answers, derive macros, and native or WASI transports.

Browser and desktop tools

  • Cua Driver + jev-use - Cua Driver example in Python and TypeScript: Jev chooses an action, the driver runs it, and code checks the result.
  • Jev Browser (MCP, CLI, library) - Playwright browser controlled by Jev, available as an MCP server, CLI, or library.
  • Jev Browser Skill - Small browser-control reference showing how to build and execute Jev action choices.
  • Jev Browser Use (existing Codex connection) - Skill that uses an existing Codex browser connection. Jev clicks and scrolls; Codex types and checks the result.
  • Jev Cua (Codex/Waku) - Mac automation using Cua Driver, with optional Jev recommendations for saved workflows.
  • Jev Social - Read-only Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn research loop: Jev Choice questions pick the platform and each bounded search, read, inspect, or finish operation; SocAI executes in the user's Chrome and the app retains source-linked evidence.
  • Jev Ultrafast - Jev picks browser actions and page elements; a separate model writes text.
  • Jev voice browser - Voice-controlled Playwright browser. Jev chooses actions from partial speech and page controls.
  • jev-bot (@compootor) - Native Mac controls through a JavaScript MCP session, with optional Jev element selection.
  • TypeSafe computer use (macOS) - Mac automation using local OCR and accessibility data, with Jev choosing the next action.

Agent tools

  • Foreman - Uses Jev to check a coding agent's progress and decide when it needs intervention.
  • Jev MCP - MCP tools for checking claims against evidence, screening content, and ranking candidates.
  • jev-belay - Claude Code Stop hook that checks local run evidence before Jev judges an unverified completion claim.
  • jev-claude-statusline - Claude Code hooks send task text, recent tool summaries, latest assistant message, and turn status to Jev (Score phase plus Noul done/waiting_on_user); answers are cached and shown as a progress segment on the Claude Code status line.
  • jev_search - Ranks files by keyword, then checks their passages with Jev in two passes. Author marks it experimental.
  • jgrep (npm: jevgrep) - Jev answers one Noul per code chunk, diff hunk, or CSV row (does this match the description?); code prints the probabilities as file:line hits, gates CI on an English rule with --diff, and lists the test files a diff can affect with --tests.
  • Oko - Code-search CLI and MCP server that finds candidates locally and uses Jev to rank the source snippets.
  • TypeSafe MCP - Go MCP server for making Jev requests from coding agents.

Apps and integrations

  • nospace - Adds spaces while you type. Jev chooses between possible word splits; a separate model handles spelling corrections.
  • tisco - Searches video transcripts with Jev, then previews clip moves and renames for approval.
  • Vibe Domain - Ranks domain names by the requested style. Has a no-key heuristic mode and a hosted Jev option.
  • Home Assistant Jev - Adds Jev decisions to Home Assistant entities and automations.
  • llm-typesafe - Use Jev from the LLM command line or Python, with stdin, templates, and sync/async calls.
  • MinusPodJev - Podcast ad-detection adapter for MinusPod: Jev scores transcript segments and code assembles the ad spans.

Games and creative projects

  • Jev Chess - A shared chess game against Jev with move probabilities. Hosted demo; source code not verified.
  • Jev Plays Snake - Snake where code finds legal moves and Jev picks a direction.
  • jev-plays-pokemon-red - Pokemon Red agent where code builds legal actions and route state; Jev chooses only at branch points.
  • JevAI for XMage - Magic: The Gathering bots that use Jev alone or alongside XMage search.
  • JevPilot - Driving simulation where Jev chooses steering and speed. Not a real-world driving system.
  • PROMPT FPS / Jev Doom - Jev chooses actions in a browser-based Doom engine. Uses Freedoom assets.
  • TypeSafe Mario - Jev picks controller inputs from emulator state. Requires a lawful local game setup.
  • Jev Music Playground - Jev picks musical parameters; code turns them into notes and MIDI. Includes an offline mode.

Independent models

  • CUA-S1-FORMS (independent specialist) - Cua's independent form-filling model and dataset. Not a general desktop agent or official Jev weights.
  • Jevlike (independent option scorer) - Independent one-pass option scorer with training code and game examples. Not TypeSafe Jev.
  • OpenJev SGLang - Independent typed-decision server using open models and SGLang. Not official Jev weights.

Supporting drivers

  • Browser Harness (supporting driver) - The CDP browser connection used by Jev Ultrafast. Model-neutral, not a Jev model.
